title: Optogenetic dephosphorylation of phosphatidylinositol 4,5 bisphosphate in Xenopus laevis oocytes
protocol: Select oocytes that are in stage IV or V of maturation.
Mix 20 ng each of CIBN-CAAX, CRY2-5-ptaseOCRL and rat Kir2.1 RNA in a tube brought up to a final volume of 1 μL with RNAse-free water.
Pull needles for microinjection to an internal diameter of 12–18 microns from glass capillaries.
Prefill the injection needle with mineral oil and then fit it onto the injection needle.
Pipette the RNA drop into the injection needle by holding down the ‘fill’ button.
Pipette oocytes onto a grid filled with OR2(+).
Inject each oocyte with 50 nL of the RNA mixture.
Incubate the oocytes for 1–2 days at +17°C in OR2(+) supplemented with 1% Penicillin/Streptomycin in a petri dish.
Pull borosilicate glass pipettes the day prior to the experiment.
Cut pipettes to 10–15 μm in diameter at the tip.
Prefill recording pipettes with filling solution containing 3 M KCl and 1.5% agarose.
Set up for TEVC by priming the perfusion apparatus.
Flush perfusion tubes with warm water.
Add low-K (96 mM Na+), high-K (96 mM K+) and 10 mM BaCl2 made up in high-K to separate reservoirs in the perfusion set-up.
Prime perfusion flow to attain a rate of 1–2 drops per second.
Adjust bath aspiration for quick exchange rate of the bath solution with the perfusate.
Orient blue light apparatus toward the oocyte recording chamber.
Open recording program WinWCP and create a -80 to +80 mV ramp protocol by navigating from Setup > Stimulus/recording protocol editor.
Set stimulus type to ‘voltage’ and the holding potential to 0 mV in the stimulus/recording protocol editor.
Change the recording duration to 360 ms, with a stimulus repeat period of 1 s and no. of records set to 10000 under the ‘Recording’ tab.
Drag AO waveforms step (П), ramp (/) and step (П) from the toolbox into the boxes under the ‘protocol’ section in the protocol editor.
Place pre-filled glass pipettes over silver electrode wires.
Lower the pipettes into the bath solution.
Compensate the pipette junction potential by turning appropriate amplifier knobs corresponding to each electrode.
Check the resistance of the electrodes on the recording amplifier, ensuring it falls within 0.2–1 MΩ range.
Place an oocyte into the recording chamber and insert both recording pipettes into the oocyte under low-K+ perfusion.
Create a new data file in WinWCP (file > new data file) and name the file.
Hit ‘record’.
Switch the perfusion to high-K+ and wait for the increase in current to stabilize.
Turn on the blue LED to activate the phosphatase after the current in high-K+ has stabilized.
Wait for the current decay following blue-light activation to reach steady-state.
Switch the perfusion to 10 mM Ba2+ in high-K+ to block Kir2.1 channels.
Allow the current following barium block to stabilize to a steady state level before ending the recording.
Chloride the silver wires used for recording as well as bath electrodes by placing them in commercial bleach for ∼5 min.
Rinse the wires in water and dry before use in experiments.
Optimize the setting on the ‘blue’ LED to attain close to 5 mW/cm² of power for optimal recruitment of the phosphatase to the oocyte membrane.
Open the file in WinWCP.
Go to analysis > waveform measurement.
Drag both olive colored cursors at the edges of the waveform window and place them over the section corresponding to the -80 mV step, away from capacitance spikes.
Click ‘Do Analysis’ on the left panel without changing other settings.
Select only ‘record’ and ‘average’ under the tables tab.
Click ‘add variable’ to populate current values in the table.
Export data to a spreadsheet using edit > copy data.
Select file > export > (output format Axon ABF) OK in Clampfit software.
Update the WinWCP software to its latest version from the University of Strathclyde website.
